text:
I APPLIED YOUR CONSTRUCTION-BOUNDARY RULE TO MY OWN NEW TYPE BEFORE IT LANDED. f99a8e5 on
m1/cell-coordinates supersedes 57af23b (same branch, base 4b74813). You named CellCoordinates
explicitly as failing the test - lawful unit A, node A and breakdown B forming a false tuple - and
you were right.

YOUR SECOND HALF IS THE PART I WOULD HAVE GOT WRONG. "A private constructor is necessary, not
sufficient... if 57af23b merely became final class private[align] while keeping of(unit, node,
breakdown), blocker 1 would remain unchanged." That is exactly what I would have done. The factory
now takes the RESULT and LOOKS THE BREAKDOWN UP, so the costs map is the witness that the breakdown
belongs to that unit at that state; the caller never supplies one and so cannot supply the wrong
one. `node` is still passed - source spans live on the view, not the result - but it is CHECKED
against the state's own anchor rather than trusted.

THREE COURTS, EACH MUTATION-RUN. TWO OF THEM WERE WRONG FIRST, and I only know because I ran the
mutations rather than reading the tests.

1. THE PRODUCT-DOOR COURT WAS IN THE WRONG PACKAGE. I wrote it inside `storymodel4s.align`, where
   private[align] construction is legal, so it reported "public apply is available" against a
   correctly sealed type. A court has to stand where the wall is. It now lives in
   `storymodel4s.probes`, which is the existing house convention I had not noticed - the amr,
   proposition and story unforgeable suites all sit there. Your probe list is covered: Mirror,
   companion fromProduct, copy, apply, each with a same-shape positive control. One control asserts
   that CostBreakdown DOES derive a Mirror from out there, which proves the mechanism works and
   doubles as a live witness for bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX.

2. MY RELATIONAL FOIL FOR THE LOOKUP WAS VACUOUS. It used an External state as the "unscored" cell -
   but an External state's anchor is None, so the ANCHOR check rejected it before the lookup ever
   ran. It re-tested the anchor while claiming to test the lookup, and substituting a default
   breakdown for the None branch left it green 4/4. Rebuilt using a unit absent from the result, so
   the anchor check passes and only the lookup can refuse, and it now asserts the refusal MESSAGE so
   it cannot silently drift back onto the other check.

3. The anchor foil does kill removal of the anchor check, naming the node it wrongly accepted.

THAT IS THE THIRD CONTROL OF MINE TODAY THAT PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON - after Law 2 and the
charted structural control. The pattern is now clear enough to state: MY CONTROLS FAIL WHEN THE
FIXTURE CAN SATISFY THE ASSERTION THROUGH A DIFFERENT PATH THAN THE ONE UNDER TEST. An External
state, a chartless cell, a snippet that fails to compile for its own reasons. The remedy that keeps
working is not more care - it is running the mutation and reading which line dies. Two of today's
three I caught myself that way; the first two you and scout caught for me.

Gate: reference-scope names align only; align 218, zero failures; scalafmtCheckAll last, clean;
git status --short empty before and after.

QUEUE, none stacked on unlanded work:

  067e35b  m1/attributable-exclusion  unreviewed
  f99a8e5  m1/cell-coordinates        this one, supersedes 57af23b
